config.title: Conditional Classes

intro.title: Conditional Classes
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple React component that toggles a visual theme, like a light or dark mode button, using conditional CSS classes. You'll learn how to apply CSS classes to JSX elements based on component state or props in React with TypeScript. The core concept involves using JavaScript expressions, such as the ternary operator or template literals, to dynamically set the className attribute. You'll work with React hooks like useState to manage state and TypeScript interfaces to define prop types, creating an interactive UI that responds to user actions.
intro.usecase: Conditional classes are essential for creating responsive, interactive interfaces in modern web applications. In dashboards, you might highlight active metrics with different colors based on thresholds, or in forms, you could show validation errors by adding error styles to invalid fields. Navigation menus frequently use conditional classes to indicate the current page by applying an 'active' class to the selected menu item. This pattern allows developers to create dynamic, user-friendly interfaces that respond to user actions and application state changes.

objectives: Apply conditional logic to dynamically assign CSS class names based on component state.
Construct a React component that renders UI elements with classes that change in response to user interactions.
Implement a TypeScript interface to define the props for a component that accepts conditional class configurations.
Manipulate component state to trigger class updates when boolean conditions change.
Integrate a utility function to compute and return a conditional class string from multiple boolean flags.
Configure event handlers to update state variables that control the visibility or styling of elements.
Render a component that visually demonstrates the applied conditional classes through dynamic styling changes.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules for building React components with state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing modules
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, enabling the use of React and the useState hook.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure you've imported both React and useState from 'react'. Check the syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX. The component should return a div element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named App that returns a JSX element. For now, just return an empty div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named App is defined and returns a div element.
successCriteria: The App component is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named App that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it App and it returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize state for active status
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, declare a state variable called 'isActive' using useState, initializing it to false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the boolean type annotation.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: boolean state initialization
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'isActive' initialized to false, ready to control conditional classes.
successCriteria: State variable 'isActive' is declared with useState
Initial value is set to false
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the boolean type annotation and initializing it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the App component, use useState<boolean>(false) to create an isActive state variable.

steps.title: Define toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a function named toggleActive that toggles the isActive state value.
steps.hint: The function should use the setter from useState to update isActive to the opposite of its current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleActive function is defined that correctly toggles the isActive boolean state.
successCriteria: The toggleActive function is defined and uses setIsActive to toggle the boolean value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You defined a function, but make sure it correctly toggles the boolean value using setIsActive.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler is missing or doesn't properly toggle the state. Try defining a function that sets isActive to the opposite of its current value.

steps.title: Add container div with conditional class
steps.instruction: In the return statement of your component, add a <div> element with a className that conditionally includes the string 'active' when isActive is true. Use a template literal with a ternary operator.
steps.hint: You can write className={`container ${isActive ? 'active' : ''}`} to conditionally add the 'active' class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div element with a className that includes 'active' only when isActive is true.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element with a className attribute using a template literal and ternary operator to conditionally add the 'active' class based on isActive.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div, but the className might not be using the correct conditional logic. Make sure to use a template literal with a ternary operator that checks isActive.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement doesn't contain a div with a conditional className. Add a <div> element with className={`container ${isActive ? 'active' : ''}`} or similar.

steps.title: Add heading inside container
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add an h1 element with the text 'Conditional Classes Demo'.
steps.hint: Add the heading element as a child inside the opening and closing tags of the div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a heading inside a container

Welcome to the App
steps.expectedOutcome: The container div now contains an h1 heading with the specified text.
successCriteria: An h1 element is present inside the container div
The h1 element contains the text 'Conditional Classes Demo'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an element, but make sure it's an h1 with exactly the text 'Conditional Classes Demo'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading wasn't added correctly. Check that you placed an h1 element with the correct text inside the div.

steps.title: Add paragraph with status text
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your component, add a paragraph element that displays 'Status: Active' when isActive is true, otherwise 'Status: Inactive'.
steps.hint:
Use a ternary operator inside curly braces within the

element to conditionally render the text based on the isActive state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional text rendering example

{isLoggedIn ? 'Welcome back!' : 'Please log in'}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element showing dynamic status text based on the isActive state value.
successCriteria:
A

element is added inside the div that conditionally displays 'Status: Active' or 'Status: Inactive' using a ternary operator with isActive.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it uses the isActive state to conditionally display the correct status text.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph with conditional status text hasn't been added correctly. Check that you're using a ternary operator with isActive inside the

element.

steps.title: Add toggle button and wire onClick
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Toggle Status' and wire its onClick event to the toggleActive handler function.
steps.hint: Remember to define the toggleActive function first if you haven't already, then add the button element with the onClick attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Toggle Status' appears in the UI that will toggle the isActive state when clicked.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Toggle Status' is present
onClick event is wired to the toggleActive handler function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the button element and wired its onClick to the toggleActive handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or event handler isn't quite right. Check that you've defined toggleActive and added onClick={toggleActive} to the button.

steps.title: Add second element with different conditional logic
steps.instruction: Add a new <div> element inside the container div that has a className of 'highlighted' only when isActive is true, using the logical AND operator (&&).
steps.hint: You can use the logical AND operator to conditionally include a class: className={isActive && 'highlighted'}. Place this new div after the existing button.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional class with logical AND
div className={isVisible && 'visible-box'}
steps.expectedOutcome: A new div element will be added that conditionally receives the 'highlighted' class based on the isActive state.
successCriteria: A new div element is added inside the container div with className={isActive && 'highlighted'} using the logical AND operator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a new div, but check if you're using the logical AND operator correctly for the className.
steps.feedbackWrong: The new div with conditional className using logical AND operator wasn't added correctly. Review the syntax for conditional classes with &&.

steps.title: Add text inside second element
steps.instruction: Inside the second div, add a span element with the text 'This is highlighted when active'.
steps.hint: Place a <span> element inside the second div, with the text content as specified.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding text inside an element This is highlighted when active
steps.expectedOutcome: The second div will contain a span element with the text 'This is highlighted when active'.
successCriteria: A span element with the text 'This is highlighted when active' is added inside the second div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an element, but make sure it's a span with the exact text 'This is highlighted when active'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second div should contain a span element with the text 'This is highlighted when active'. Check your syntax and placement.
